findings.claim: A projectId belonging to another organization is given two different, mutually exclusive answers: requirement 9 says 400 with projectUnavailable, and the POST …/requests contract says 404 and 'never 403'.

witness.detail: A `user` in org A posts POST /api/organizations/A/requests with a projectId that exists in org B. Requirement 9 (line 96): 'A project that is archived, or belongs to another organization, is rejected with 400 and `REQUEST_MESSAGES.projectUnavailable`.' The POST contract (line 487): '`404` for a project or membership outside the caller's organization — never 403.' One implementation answers 400 {"error":"validation_error","fields":{"projectId":"That project is not available"}}; the other answers 404 with the not-found body. No test case decides it: TC-01-INT-15 covers only the archived project (400 projectUnavailable) and TC-01-INT-06 covers only the cross-org membership (404). Whichever the implementer picks, they will write the integration case that pins it, and QA will confirm the implementer's guess rather than the spec.

findings.suggestedFix: Pick one and state it in both places. The cross-org membership already answers 404 'so ids cannot be probed across organizations' (requirement 13); the same argument applies to a project id, which suggests amending requirement 9 to say 400 projectUnavailable for an ARCHIVED project in the caller's organization and 404 for one outside it — then add the second half to TC-01-INT-15.

findings.claim: The `status` query parameter of GET …/requests already has a different, incompatible vocabulary that filters the vacation feed. Requirement 42 replaces it and the contract makes an unknown value a 400, but nothing says how — or whether — the vacation section is filtered afterwards, and the answer changes what a manager sees on a page that ships today.

witness.detail: Today `GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests?status=…` accepts pending | approved | rejected | cancelled | all, defaults to 'pending', and silently falls back rather than erroring (packages/validation/src/index.ts:1878-1897, consumed at apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts). apps/api/test/requests-page.spec.ts:301-320 asserts that filtering; apps/web/src/layout/requests-badge-context.tsx sends status=pending. Requirement 42 (line 195) redefines the same parameter as all | open | answered | granted | declined | cancelled, and the contract (line 468) says '400 for an unknown status or type value' — so `pending` becomes a 400, while `cancelled` remains valid and now means a cancelled *request*. Concrete divergence: an organization has one PENDING and one REJECTED vacation request; a manager opens /org/{orgId}/requests with no filter. Implementation A applies `status` to Request rows only and renders the spec-10 feed unfiltered — two vacation cards, where today the manager sees one. Implementation B keeps a separate vacation status filter — one card, but then the endpoint accepts a value requirement 42's closed set excludes. Both satisfy the text; they differ in what is on the screen and in whether a manager can still narrow the vacation section to pending at all, which is the only thing that page does today. Backward Compatibility 3 ('VacationRequest is not touched — not a column, not a query') claims the second and requirement 42 claims the first.

findings.suggestedFix: State in requirement 41 or 42 whether `status` and `type` apply to the vacation section, what the section shows by default, and what replaces today's Pending-only default view — then say explicitly that the spec-10 status vocabulary is retired on this endpoint and name apps/api/test/requests-page.spec.ts:301-320 as the assertion that changes with it.

findings.claim: Requirement 23 restricts `answered` to the addressee or an admin, but the spec defines no status and no message for refusing anyone else — the Error Messages table has notYoursToGrant, notYoursToDecline and notYoursToCancel and no answer row, and the transition contract lists only those three 403s.

witness.detail: Sam (role `user`) raises a request addressed to the admin and then posts POST /api/organizations/{orgId}/requests/{id}/answer. Sam is a party to the request, so 404 (line 517's 'when not party') does not apply; the row is `open`, so alreadyTerminal and invalidTransition do not apply; and requirement 23 forbids the write. Line 517 lists the available refusals: '403 …notYoursToGrant / …notYoursToDecline / …notYoursToCancel'. None fits. Implementation A invents REQUEST_MESSAGES.notYoursToAnswer with text no table specifies — text review will then flag it as a user-facing string absent from the spec. Implementation B reuses notYoursToDecline ('Only the person this is addressed to can decline it') on an answer route. Implementation C returns 404 and makes a request the caller can see unanswerable-and-invisible at the same time. All three are observable and different, and no test case covers the row.

findings.suggestedFix: Add a `notYoursToAnswer` row to the Error Messages table with its exact text and route, add it to the transition contract's 403 list beside the other three, and add the case to TC-01-INT-08 (which today probes grant only).

findings.claim: AC-3 and Backward Compatibility 5, read literally, forbid requirements 37 and 38 and the case that asserts them.

witness.detail: AC-3: 'No role sees a request, a vacation row, or a control that it cannot see before this spec ships.' README Backward Compatibility 5: 'No role gains visibility of anything it cannot see today.' Requirement 38 makes the sidebar Requests row render for every signed-in member, and TC-01-E2E-10 asserts it is present for all four roles, citing a measured count of 0 for a `user` before this spec. A `user` therefore gains a nav row, a page and their own request rows. The plan reads both criteria as being about pre-existing DATA — vacation rows and other people's requests — which is how their named observers (TC-01-INT-18, TC-01-E2E-08) test them.

findings.suggestedFix: Narrow AC-3 to 'no role sees a vacation row, or a request it is not party to, that it cannot see today' so the criterion and requirement 38 stop disagreeing on paper.

findings.claim: The blast radius reads as though REQUEST_MESSAGES were a new export; it already exists and holds spec 09's vacation-request strings.

witness.detail: '**`packages/validation`.** Three new capabilities in `MemberCapability` **and** `Capability`, plus `REQUEST_MESSAGES`.' The const is defined at packages/validation/src/index.ts:1746 with 21 spec-09 keys (startInPast, insufficientBalance, cancelForbidden, reviewForbidden, …) and is imported by apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/page.tsx and packages/validation/src/vacation-requests.test.ts. None of this spec's 30 keys collides with them, so the plan extends the existing const in place; a rename would touch every vacation call site, which this spec forbids.

findings.suggestedFix: Say 'extends `REQUEST_MESSAGES` (packages/validation/src/index.ts:1746, spec 09's) with 30 keys' so the next reader does not create a second export.

findings.claim: Requirement 43's comparator and TC-01-UNIT-04's stated principle agree only for the row configuration the case happens to describe.

witness.detail: Requirement 43 orders by 'blocking and non-terminal first, then overdue, then priority descending, then lastActivityAt descending' — there is no key that says terminal rows sort last. TC-01-UNIT-04 expects 'the terminal row sorts below every non-terminal one despite being blocking', which the literal comparator delivers only because the case's terminal row is neither overdue nor (implicitly) high-priority. Rows [granted+urgent, open+normal] sort granted-first under the requirement and last under the case's principle.

findings.suggestedFix: Either add 'non-terminal before terminal' as the first sort key in requirement 43, or fix the terminal row's priority and lastActivityAt in TC-01-UNIT-04 so the case tests the comparator as written.

findings.claim: `counts.total` is undefined, and `type=vacation` has no stated effect on the `requests[]` array.

witness.detail: The response carries `"counts": { "waitingOnMe": 1, "total": 3 }` and no requirement says whether `total` is org-wide or the count matching the active filters — today's equivalent, `totalCount`, is deliberately computed from the unfiltered set (apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts). Requirement 42 admits `type=vacation` while requirement 41 says vacation rows are not `Request` rows in this release, so the filter selects a section rather than filtering the array. The plan mirrors today's unfiltered `total` and treats `type=vacation` as an empty `requests[]` plus the unchanged vacation block.

findings.suggestedFix: State both in the API contract — one sentence each.
